newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Queensland Australia seen facing average rain.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Queensland Australia seen facing average rain.

text.p: Forecasts continued to suggest a high probability of near average rainfall for most of the Australian state of Queensland in the March to May period, Queensland's Department of Primary Industries said.
A cyclone off Queensland's coast could bring further rainfall to coastal and inland areas within the next week, it said in a statement.
Above average rainfall at the end of February in the Mt Isa and Cloncurry areas of the central west resulted in major flooding in the Leichhardt and Cloncurry river systems, it said.
Cyclones Gillian and Ita also caused flooding in the Mackay and Moura areas earlier in the month, it said.
Above average rainfall at the end of January and in the first few days of February caused major flooding in southern central regions, it said.
Many parts of northern, western and central Queensland received good falls of rain in February and were well-placed for the winter months, it said.
Although most areas of the state had received some rainfall in January and February, isolated pockets missed out and would need good rainfall in March to halt a return to drought conditions, it said.

Southern coastal areas around Dalby and Kingaroy, and between Rockhampton and Marlborough on the north coast, had received very little beneficial rainfall in January and February and required rain urgently to secure a season for 1997, it said,
